subject: Why Evidence Matters in the Age of Alternative Facts
posts:
Debating evidence in elite echo chambers. A boundary error: treating academic panels as public education while ignoring the root causes of systemic distrust.

Why Evidence Matters
Evidence: science-guided policy, academic panels, public trust repair

Academics claim that hosting public discussions on scientific evidence will restore the authority of facts and ensure evidence guides democratic decisions.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

These panels remain insular academic events, reinforcing the status of the speakers without addressing why the public has lost faith in elite institutions.
Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, -1.0) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
By framing academic panels as solutions to public distrust, institutions convert systemic credibility crises into self-validating seminars, leaving the real gap unaddressed.
The LSE Festival is hosting a panel discussion featuring journalists and academics to debate how scientific evidence can guide public decisions in an age of 'alternative facts' and skepticism.

The Bright Side:
Documentation of evidence-based policy is vital, and these discussions can clarify standards of proof for researchers and policymakers.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
They claim this is a logical issue of 'facts' (WHAT). It is actually a historical crisis of trust and exclusion (CAUSE/EFFECT).

It is a bait-and-switch: promising public outreach, delivering elite validation.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between restoring broad public trust and holding exclusive academic panel discussions...

...it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. The academic community secures its own prestige while leaving the public sphere increasingly polarized. With υ at -1.0 and ψ at -1.0, the trust gap widens.

The Unavoidable Truth: Trust is built on institutional integrity and results, not just debating facts.

The Unavoidable Lie: That the public rejects science simply because they lack access to academic panels.

Alethekanon:
Credibility cannot be lectured into existence. When academic institutions ignore their own complicity in policy failures, their defense of 'evidence' functions as class gatekeeping. Real trust requires material accountability.

Awwthekanon:
It is so disheartening when people can't agree on basic truths, and it makes sense that scholars want to help. But we need to listen to why people feel left out and build bridges of understanding, not walls of intellect.

Brothekanon:
So the plan to cure 'alternative facts' is to have a bunch of professors talk to other professors on Bluesky? Good luck with that, bros. If you want people to believe the data, you gotta show it works in the real world.

Synthesized Resolution Vector:
Blended Path: The Path of Deception — Aletheia blends Bro's check and Aww's empathy, concluding that lecturing on facts fails to repair systemic institutional distrust.
Final Coordinates: (-1.0, -1.0)
